column1: # The latest independent audit of each table: an auditor who did not write the entries drew a random sample of rows graded understood
# and re-derived each from the binaries or the cited specification. real = the entry held up, shallow = true but derived from a name or
# credited without behaviour of its own, wrong = contradicted. sample is small: read it with the percentage. The last row of a table with
# the latest date is the one summary.tsv and docs/coverage.md show.

column7: PIC page: 12 claims re-derived from pic.o, pcibr.o and the IP35 PROM; wrong: an unknown part and revision is not rejected (only the debug name changes), and the PROM interrupt-register clear writes 64-bit zero and all-ones to +0x108 and +0x110 on the PIC path (the 32-bit stores at +0x10c, +0x114 and +0x12c are the non-PIC path); shallow: the PIO flush workaround omitted the counter address, the value 1, and the device and pin-mask conditions; also fixed an inverted order of the revision-1 enable clear and the unlisted control-register mask. Census mechanics: 4 of 4 PIC sites right

Bedrock page: 8 claims re-derived from kernel.o and its neighbours; wrong: hub_error_clear (all-ones writes counted as zeroes, 15 slots not 14, two aliases), the +0x1604200 counter reading (bits 13:4 times five at all 52 sites), and the +0x1000090 store attribution (sites belong to symbol-less neighbours); shallow: per_hub_init omitted the slice stores in the second window. Also outside the sample: hub_widget_reset had a loop over eight registers and no polling (wrong), kernel.o has 61 not 71 window literals (wrong). Census mechanics: 4 of 6 Bedrock sites exact, 2 with a dropped run-time displacement or loop-iteration artifact; gp auto-min holds in 11 of 11 objects

Xbow page: 12 claims re-derived from the IP27 xbow.o routines xbow_enable_perf_counter, xbow_reset_link, xbow_prio_bw_alloc and xbow_errintr_handler; all held. Outside the sample: the bandwidth refusal test named the wrong register (the compared byte count is the request rounded to register units and converted back, not the raw request in a3) and was corrected. 8 further claims drawn from the PIC and Bedrock pages (pic_attach2, md_int_block, hubni_print_state) held too

IOC3 page: 4 claims re-derived from ioc3ei.o, ioc3.o and if_ef.o (eiattach writes to 0x38, 0x34 and 0x2c; ioc3_init registration; the MII routines; ioc3_error_handler); shallow: ioc3_error_handler was described as writing 0x40 back, it stores the constant 1 after a valid-bit test and a 13-way jump on bits 4:1. scripts/facts.py failed on that routine (a symbolic table base was formatted as a number); fixed and tested

IOC4 page: 4 claims re-derived from ioc4_pckm.o, sio_ioc4.o and ide.o (the keyboard control store, hardware_init ring bases, ioc4_dma_error_intr, xide_intr_clear with the ATA accessor stride); wrong: the error-address low word's unit is bits 4:2 doubled and added to the character 1, and bit 1 picks the printed word RX or TX, not bits 3:1 as a unit

Bridge and XBridge page: 8 claims re-derived from pcibr.o, xbridge.o and the IP27 kernel; wrong: xbridge_attach does not clear bit 24 of the interrupt enable (the literal 0x00003eff7ffffe00 is ORed in whole; the 0xc0023 test sets record fields), and part 0xd100 tested by xbow_widget_present is read from the crossbar's own identification word, not a Bridge-family chip; shallow: the upper bus error address accessor applies no 15:0 mask
